$schema_note: AUTHORED. The two street faces N. Roswell Gifford draws beside the first Tremont House, read building by building off the drawing and expanded into one structure record per building by tools/generate_gifford_street_faces.py, which tools/check.sh re-derives byte for byte. Widths, storeys, roof forms, fronts and the order along each face are READINGS of the drawing; every metre is still reconstructed, because the drawing carries no scale.

owner_ruling.what_it_rules: The drawing is read as a view of the town on 1 July 1835, although it is retrospective and may show the street as it stood up to the 1839 fire. That reading is the owner's and is recorded as liberty L-gifford-street-faces-3605 in docs/LIBERTIES.md; it supersedes, for these two faces only, the source record's earlier note that nothing in the dataset may take a position from the plate.

camera.how: The image-gate camera solved on the Tremont House (3.5 px RMS on six envelope corners) is in the hotel's own footprint frame. Carried into the town through the hotel's placement (its pictured gable, the one carrying the name, on Lake Street and its pictured long side on Dearborn: rotation 270 about the Lake and Dearborn corner), the eye stands south-east of the crossing looking west-north-west, at local E 723.5 m, N -148.1 m, 2.4 m up, heading 298.2 degrees. Through it the drawing's left-hand row is the north side of Lake Street running west from the hotel, and its right-hand row the west side of Dearborn running north. The near stores of both rows land at 5-7.5 m frontages through this camera, which is what a party-line store of the period measured; the far end of the Lake row is drawn compressed (the camera would put its first stores 14-16 m wide and its end across Clark Street, which the drawing does not show), so the far stores keep the drawn ORDER and FORM and take frontages in proportion to their bay counts, and the row is fitted between Clark Street and the hotel.
